model_claims.text: Evaluating every rotation condition prevents a skipped condition from firing spuriously.
model_claims.source_quote: Evaluate every rotation condition so a skipped one cannot fire spuriously

model_claims.text: A skipped condition leaves a stale _limit in the past, causing it to fire on the very next logged message and produce a spurious extra rotation.
model_claims.source_quote: A skipped condition is left holding a limit that is now in the past, and it therefore fires on the **very next logged message** — producing a second, immediate, spurious rotation.

model_claims.text: After the change, all rotation conditions are evaluated even after one returns True, preserving the side‑effect of limit updates.
model_claims.source_quote:
# Note that the conditions must all be evaluated, even after one of them returned
# True, because "RotationTime" instances keep their limit up-to-date as a side-effect
# of being called. Skipping them would leave a stale limit in the past, causing a
# spurious extra rotation on the next logged message.
should_rotate = False
for rotation in self._rotations:
    if rotation(message, file):
        should_rotate = True
return should_rotate

model_claims.text: The return value still indicates true if any rotation condition is true, preserving the "any of which can trigger the rotation" contract.
model_claims.source_quote: This keeps the documented "any of which can trigger the rotation" contract for the return value while restoring the side effect the conditions rely on.

model_claims.text: The test test_multiple_rotation_conditions_all_evaluated fails before the change (assert 3 == 2) and passes after the change.
model_claims.source_quote:
`test_multiple_rotation_conditions_all_evaluated` is added to `tests/test_filesink_rotation.py`.
- Fails before the change with `assert 3 == 2`; passes after.

model_rejected_claims.text: Using any() over a generator short-circuits, causing remaining rotation conditions to never be invoked and their _limit not advanced.
model_rejected_claims.source_quote: any() over a generator **short-circuits**. That is fine for the return value, but each `RotationTime` condition is *stateful*: it lazily computes `self._limit` on first call and then advances it as a side effect of being invoked ... When the first condition returns `True`, the remaining conditions are never invoked, so their `_limit` is never advanced past the current time.

model_rejected_claims.text: With rotation conditions ["13:00", "12:00"], a file created at 06:00 and two messages logged at 13:00:01 results in exactly two log files after the fix (instead of three before).
model_rejected_claims.source_quote:
Message "b" legitimately rotates at 13:00:01; "c" should not.
